There are three ways to record a video of a page, and each gives something up.

record on (help record) records the selected tab's page from inside the browser: headless, hidden and
background tabs too, with nothing to set up but ffmpeg. It has no pointer and no browser toolbars. For
quick clips, and for an agent recording its own work.

A screen recorder on the person's machine (OBS, ffmpeg -f x11grab, macOS screencapture -v) records their
screen as they see it, pointer included, smooth and in real time. It records the screen or a window, not
a tab: size the window, and crop off the toolbars, for just the page. Ask before starting one, or have
them start it. It cannot see a headless browser: for a browser of the REPL's own, --launch --headed on a
screen. For a polished video of a person's browser.

Microsoft's playwright-cli (the npm package @playwright/cli; video-start and video-stop) records a
browser of its own, not this one, which starts logged out. For a scripted flow in a clean browser.
